signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.49 remains structurally supported by a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential despite recent price softening. While speculative positioning remains heavily net short JPY at -63,633 (COT LF), the options market has aggressively shifted to price downside protection. The 25d RR at -2.20 reflects an extreme put skew, the strongest directional bias in the G10 space, signaling that institutional desks are paying a high premium to hedge against a JPY recovery. This divergence between crowded carry positioning and defensive options pricing suggests a vulnerable bull trend, especially as Japanese bond yields rise on expectations for faster BoJ policy normalization. The pair trades below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (161.24/161.17/158.07), confirming a loss of technical momentum. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; options market hedging suggests carry unwind risk. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 18 Sep — hold pricing dominant. Risk: US CPI surprise re-ignites Fed hike pricing and widens the nominal yield gap.

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard identifies a bilateral theme in CAD/JPY with a 0.904% performance spread over the last week. CAD leads G10 performance (+0.439% avg) while JPY laggards (-0.465% avg), even as CAD faces a carry disadvantage of +125bp relative to JPY's lower policy rate. This outperformance is supported by a moderate positive bias in the Canadian Economic Surprise Index (+12.0) compared to a broader softening in G10 peers. Technical levels show CAD/JPY benefiting from USD/CAD trading below its SMA20 and SMA50 cluster at 1.4055/1.4071, reflecting CAD's relative resilience. The Hormuz reopening headlines further complicate the energy-linked CAD outlook, though the bilateral G10 theme currently overrides commodity-specific volatility. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; G10 momentum favors the CAD leader against the JPY laggard. Catalyst: Next BoC meeting on 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: JPY safe-haven demand on renewed Hormuz uncertainty compresses the G10 performance spread.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Real Rate Support
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3502 trades with a significant volatility risk premium (VRP) of +4.9%, where ATM IV at 11.0% sharply exceeds the HV30 of 6.1%. This elevated protection pricing indicates the options market is anticipating higher realized volatility than the recent trend suggests, aligning with BBH's view that soft GDP is likely to trigger a dovish BoE repricing. Despite this, GBP maintains a restrictive real rate of +0.93% and neutral carry vs USD (0bp spread). COT positioning shows speculative net longs at +39,039 (70.1% long), reflecting institutional confidence that has kept the pair above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3412/1.3366/1.3406). The combination of crowded positioning and high vol premiums suggests an asymmetric risk profile if UK macro data misses expectations. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; high vol premium makes adding to longs expensive. Catalyst: UK Q2 GDP release this week. Risk: Strong GDP beat forces a short-squeeze in vol and targets 1.3600.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT-Retail Divergence + RBA Hawkish Risk
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7075, holding above its SMA20 and SMA50 cluster at 0.7000/0.7002, supported by a -60bp carry advantage relative to the USD. A clear divergence is active between institutional and retail sentiment: COT LF net long +37,990 (72.1% long) vs a retail extreme of 78% short. This indicates retail traders are unsuccessfully fading a trend that institutional specs are actively chasing. Commerzbank identifies hawkish risk ahead of the RBA, which may validate the institutional long bias despite a negative Economic Surprise Index of -12.2. The real policy rate of +0.60% remains restrictive, providing structural support against a US dollar that is currently underperforming the G10 average (-0.412%). Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional positioning and carry favor further upside against retail shorts. Catalyst: RBA meeting 11 Aug — 100% hold priced. Risk: RBA adopts a dovish tone on data-dependence, triggering a long-unwind toward 0.6925.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance vs Accommodative Real Rate
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5896 is supported by the strongest G10 Economic Surprise Index (+24.4), reflecting a sustained run of data beats. This fundamental strength offsets a highly accommodative real policy rate of -1.56% (nominal 2.5% vs 4.06% inflation expectations), the lowest in the G10. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. Price action is currently constructive, with the pair holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5836/0.5790/0.5829). While retail sentiment is 76% short, aligning with the COT short bias, the record of economic beats suggests the fundamental outlook is improving faster than positioning reflects. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; data outperformance targets a squeeze of spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — Hike bias priced. Risk: RBNZ pauses the hiking cycle early, validating the spec short position.
